project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Ran the self-contained runner in the project container. Unpatched: `file path opened by : webroot/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini` -> `RESULT: VULNERABLE` -> POV_EXIT=0. Independent trace via Utils.normalizePath+urlDecode+removeDots confirmed backslash traversal is preserved while forward-slash "/../.." payloads are neutralized (collapse to "/secret.txt"). Applied a representative fix (adding `.replace('\\','/')` before removeDots at StaticHandlerImpl.java:138), reran: `file path opened by : webroot/windows/win.ini` -> `RESULT: not vulnerable` -> POV_EXIT=1, then reverted the product code (verified byte-identical to original, git shows only .security-pipeline/ untracked).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code the POV recompiles vertx-web, invokes the genuine StaticHandlerImpl.handle() with request normalisedPath "/%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cwindows%5Cwin.ini", captures the path passed to FileSystem.exists() as "webroot/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini", determines that this path escapes the web root when '\' is treated as a separator, prints "RESULT: VULNERABLE", and exits 0. After a correct patch (normalizing/rejecting backslash traversal, e.g. so the handler resolves "webroot/windows/win.ini" or null), the captured path stays within the web root, the POV prints "RESULT: not vulnerable" and exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: JDK 8, Maven build. run_pov.sh recompiles the (possibly patched) vertx-web module from source and rederives the dependency classpath each run, so it always reflects the current product code. It prefers offline maven and falls back to online if needed (local ~/.m2 was seeded by `mvn -pl vertx-web -am install -DskipTests`, already done in this worktree). The filesystem-level exploit only escapes on a Windows host (where '\' is the separator); since the pipeline container is Linux, the POV faithfully reproduces the vulnerable code path by capturing the exact filesystem argument StaticHandlerImpl produces and evaluating it under Windows separator semantics, rather than relying on Linux to follow the traversal. Helper files in the same dir: Explore.java (payload trace, not used by the runner), cp.txt/compile.log (generated build artifacts).
parsed_output.regression_hint: The POV distinguishes vulnerable vs fixed by the file path StaticHandlerImpl resolves for the encoded-backslash request: vulnerable code yields a path containing ".." components that escape the web root when '\' is a separator (exit 0); a correct fix neutralizes or rejects backslash traversal so the resolved path stays under the web root or handling stops before the filesystem call (exit 1). A valid fix must strip/normalize '\' path separators (or reject them) in the StaticHandler normalization path, not merely on the forward-slash form.
parsed_output.summary: Created an end-to-end proof-of-vulnerability for CWE-022 path traversal in io.vertx.ext.web.handler.impl.StaticHandlerImpl (vertx-web 3.5.3.CR1). A request URL that percent-encodes Windows path separators (%5C == '\') survives the handler's normalization chain `Utils.removeDots(Utils.urlDecode(context.normalisedPath(), false))`, because removeDots only collapses forward-slash "../" sequences. The POV drives the real StaticHandlerImpl.handle() with the malicious path and intercepts the exact file string the handler hands to FileSystem.exists(): `webroot/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini`. Interpreting that string the way a Windows filesystem does (backslash is a separator) shows it escapes the configured web root, disclosing arbitrary files.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In StaticHandlerImpl.handle(), the single-line normalization `String path = Utils.removeDots(Utils.urlDecode(context.normalisedPath(), false));` was split so that, after url-decoding and before removeDots, backslashes are replaced with forward slashes (`path = path.replace('\\', '/')`) when the decoded path is non-null. This is null-safe (urlDecode may return null, and removeDots already tolerates null). Effect: the malicious request "/%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cwindows%5Cwin.ini" now decodes to "/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini", becomes "//../../../../windows/win.ini", and removeDots collapses the leading traversal at the root boundary, yielding "webroot/windows/win.ini" — inside the web root. Added two regression tests to StaticHandlerTest: testCantEscapeWebRootWithEncodedBackslash (encoded-backslash traversal returns 404) and testEncodedBackslashSeparatorsAreNormalized (which distinguishes patched vs unpatched: "/somedir%5C..%5Cotherpage.html" now resolves to /otherpage.html and returns 200, whereas unpatched code left the literal backslash path that does not exist -> 404). Verified: POV run_pov.sh now prints "file path opened by: webroot/windows/win.ini", "RESULT: not vulnerable", exit 1 (was exit 0/VULNERABLE before). Full StaticHandlerTest suite: 58 tests, 0 failures.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Minimal, focused change confined to the static file handler's request-path normalization; no API or dependency changes. Behavioral note: backslashes in request paths are now treated as path separators for dot-segment removal within StaticHandler. This is the intended hardening and matches how filesystems on Windows interpret such paths; it does not affect legitimate forward-slash URLs. Any (unusual) client relying on literal backslash characters being preserved verbatim in a served filename would now see them normalized to '/', but such paths previously could not be reliably or safely resolved anyway. The regression test command must run with network access (the reactor resolves vertx-web-client from Maven Central); the container's fully-offline mode lacks that artifact.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal in StaticHandlerImpl. Requests whose URLs percent-encode Windows path separators (%5C == '\') bypassed the handler's dot-segment normalization: Utils.removeDots only collapses forward-slash "../" sequences, so a decoded path like "/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini" survived intact and escaped the configured web root on platforms where '\' is a separator. The fix normalizes backslashes to forward slashes in StaticHandlerImpl.handle() before removeDots, so backslash-based traversal is collapsed within the web root exactly like forward-slash traversal.

Null-safe (urlDecode may return null; removeDots tolerates null) and targets exactly the reported sink chain (urlDecode -> removeDots -> getFile -> fs.exists). parsed_output.summary: The patch is a minimal, appropriate CWE-022 fix: in StaticHandlerImpl.handle() it normalizes backslash path separators to forward slashes (null-safe) before Utils.removeDots, so percent-encoded Windows-separator traversal (%5C == '\') collapses within the web root instead of escaping it. I independently confirmed the POV reproduces on the original source (exit 0, VULNERABLE) and no longer reproduces on the patched source (exit 1, resolved path stays in webroot), and the StaticHandlerTest regression suite passes (58/58).
